brief: 5 readability rules every designer breaks — and what to do instead in 2026.

slots.body: Five broken rules and modern fixes every interface designer needs for 2026.

slots.title: Readability Is Not
slots.body: Every year designers sacrifice clarity for aesthetics. In 2026, the rules have evolved—here are the five mistakes still breaking interfaces everywhere.
slots.quote: Legibility is the price of admission.

slots.title: Kill the Ultra
slots.body: Hairline fonts dissolve on OLED screens and in sunlight. Modern displays reward substance, so set body text no lighter than 400 regular.
slots.quote: If you can't read it in daylight, it doesn't exist.

slots.title: Gray Text Is
slots.body: Low-contrast grey feels elegant until users squint. Aim for a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1—elegance should never compete with accessibility.
slots.quote: Subtlety is not an excuse for invisibility.

slots.title: Centered Body Copy
slots.body: Center-aligned paragraphs create ragged eye movements and fatigue. Keep headlines centered, but let body copy breathe along a strong left edge.

slots.title: Tight Line Height
slots.body: A line-height of 1.2 belongs in print, not pixels. For screens, give your type room—1.5 to 1.7 lets ascenders and descenders sing without collision.
slots.quote: White space is a cognitive lubricant.

slots.title: Paragraphs Need Real
slots.body: Indentation is old school; modern interfaces need clear paragraph spacing. Add breathing room between blocks instead of forcing indent traditions.
